index_record.dataset_generation_caption:
The figure presents a hierarchical taxonomy tree for mechanical metamaterials, structured as a top-down flowchart. At the root, the term 'Metamaterials' is placed at the top center in a rectangular box. From this node, two main branches extend downward: 'Mechanical metamaterials' on the left and 'Other types' on the right. The 'Other types' branch further splits into four parallel rectangular boxes aligned vertically, labeled 'Acoustic metamaterials', 'Thermal metamaterials', 'Electronical metamaterials', and 'Optical metamaterials', each connected by a single arrow from the parent node.

The primary focus of the diagram is the 'Mechanical metamaterials' branch, which subdivides into five distinct property categories arranged horizontally: 'Tunable property', 'Negative property', 'Programmable property', 'Topology property', and 'Extreme property'. Each of these categories is represented by a rectangular box with black borders and centered text.

Under 'Tunable property', three subcategories are listed: 'Modulus', 'Strength', and 'Toughness'. These further branch into specific mechanisms or structural features. For 'Modulus', the sub-features are 'Stretch-dominated', 'Bending-dominated', 'Connectivity', 'Truss waviness', 'Disorder', and 'Hierarchy', each in a vertical rectangular box. Similarly, 'Strength' and 'Toughness' do not have further subdivisions shown.

The 'Negative property' category branches into 'Negative stiffness', 'Negative Poisson's ratio', and 'Negative thermal expansion'. Under 'Negative stiffness', the mechanisms listed are 'Instability', 'Pre-stressed lattices', and 'Snap-through structure'. Under 'Negative Poisson's ratio', the mechanisms include 'Kinkami-based', 'Origami-based', 'Chirality', 'Re-entrant structure', 'Pattern transformation', 'Square twist', and 'bi-material lattice'. 'Negative thermal expansion' has no further subdivisions.

The 'Programmable property' and 'Topology property' nodes do not have any further branches or subcategories shown in the diagram.

The 'Extreme property' node branches into two subcategories: 'Pentamodes' and 'Extreme stiffness'. 'Pentamodes' further branches into four responsive mechanisms: 'Swelling', 'Thermal responsive', 'Chemical responsive', and 'Optical responsive'. 'Extreme stiffness' branches into four structural approaches: 'High connectivity', 'Stretching dominated', 'Wall based', and 'TMPS'.

All connections between nodes are represented by solid black arrows pointing downward, indicating a hierarchical relationship from general to specific. All boxes are uniformly styled with thin black borders, white fill, and black sans-serif text. The layout is strictly horizontal and vertical, forming a clear tree structure. The figure is designed to illustrate a curated taxonomy for internal inductive bias extraction in mechanical metamaterials, as stated in the caption.
